messages.subject: Re: Export labels rather than IDs in results stats file
parts:
Barry:

I'm afraid that would involve quite a re-write of the "innards" of=20
Distance. You should also recognise that there is uncertainty=20
associated with the estimates of density on each of your samples. So=20
propagating that uncertainty into your ANOVA is a bigger problem than=20
the labelling of the output.

You might want to look at
Buckland, S.T., Russell, R.E., Dickson, B.G., Saab, V.A., Gorman, D.N. &=20
Block, W.M. (2009) Analyzing Designed Experiments in Distance Sampling.=20
/Journal of Agricultural, Biological, and Environmental Statistics/,=20
*14*, 432=E2=80=93442.


On 16/11/2012 17:48, Barry Robinson wrote:
> > Is there any way to have the label of the strata and samples exported i=
n the results stats file rather than the ID numbers that are assigned by =
the Distance Software when importing the data?
> >
> > I've conducted a survey that has both spatial and temporal stratificati=
on: 9 different strata sampled over 3 years. I have many samples (transec=
ts) for each strata from each year. I've used the MCDS engine to estimate=
density for each sample, so that I can export the density estimates and =
conduct a two-way ANOVA with an interaction to determine if density varie=
s across strata and/or years. To do this, I've exported the restuls stats=
file where the rows of the stats are organized by the stratum and sample=
IDs that are assigned by the Distance software when importing the data. =
However, because the year variable cannot be exported within this stats f=
ile (Distance allows stratification only by one variable and I've chosen =
to use my spatial strata), it is important that the density estimates be =
linked with the original sample label, so that I can determine which year=
each sample came from.
> >
> > Please reply to Barry Robinson: bgro...@ualberta.ca
> >
> > Thanks for your time
